text:
omar: heads up — we're seeing a spike of GPU node provisioning failures in eu-west-1. kubelet logs show image pulls failing with DNS errors: 'Name or service not known'. Any ideas?

jia: saw the alert, looking. Is this only in eu-west?

omar: yes, prod eu-west only. staging/na are fine. error happens during init when pulling images from internal registry: `registry.internal.redwood:5000`

alex: can you paste a `dig`/`nslookup` from one of the failing nodes? also paste `/etc/resolv.conf`

omar: pasted below from a failing GPU host (shortened):
```
$ cat /etc/resolv.conf
search service.local redwood.internal
nameserver 10.1.2.3
nameserver 8.8.8.8
options ndots:1

$ dig +short registry.internal.redwood @10.1.2.3
; (no answer)

$ dig +short registry.internal.redwood @8.8.8.8
93.184.216.34
```

katie: hmm that looks like split-horizon: internal names should resolve to internal IPs via 10.1.2.3 but the stub resolver is falling back to 8.8.8.8 and returning public record. Why would the stub query 8.8.8.8 if internal nameserver is primary?

alex: check `ndots` and search behavior. NDOTS=1 will try short names first, and if search list is applied it might send a query that the internal forwarder rejects, causing the client to try the next server. Also check timeouts on 10.1.2.3 — if it's slow, glibc resolver might try the next nameserver.

omar: `ndots:1` is set on these nodes. but the weird bit is 10.1.2.3 is authoritative for `internal.redwood` and is responsive in other hosts. On these GPU nodes the resolver sometimes returns SERVFAIL from 10.1.2.3.

sre-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-2106 DNS resolution failures eu-west-1 (priority P2) :link_for_ticket:

jia: are these GPU nodes using a different egress path / NAT gateway? we've recently changed SNAT policy for the gpu-subnet to use a NAT pool with source port mangling for conntrack scale. Could be stateful device dropping fragmented UDP responses.

alex: good call — UDP truncation + fallback to TCP or retry could produce inconsistent responses. if internal forwarder responds with truncated UDP, the resolver should retry over TCP but some clients don't. Can you capture tcpdump of DNS on the node?

omar: captured a short trace. summary: queries to 10.1.2.3 return UDP with TC=1 sometimes -> then node issues retry to 8.8.8.8 rather than TCP to 10.1.2.3. NAT device logs show lots of ephemeral port collisions and ICMP unreachable from upstream resolver cluster.

katie: sounds like NAT port exhaustion or port collision due to high ephemeral reuse from container runtime. GPU nodes use bursty image pulls and many concurrent DNS queries. If SNAT is reusing ports aggressively, replies might land on the wrong flow.

alex: workaround: force glibc resolver to prefer TCP for DNS by setting `options use-vc`? that's a per-host change and not ideal. Another quick mitigation is to change resolv.conf search order to put `redwood.internal` first and set `ndots:5` to avoid accidental fallback to public name. But that will increase lookup latency.

omar: can we push a kernel/sysctl tweak or iptables rule on NAT to preserve per-flow ports? I can ping infra to check if NAT config can be relaxed.

jia: infra confirmed NAT pool was shrunk last week due to cost optimization. That increased port reuse. Rolling it back should reduce collisions. They recommended increasing SNAT port range and enabling deterministic source port allocation per iptables `--random-fully` off.

katie: also we should update node bootstrap to set `options ndots:2` and explicit search order so short internal names resolve locally before public. That avoids hitting external resolvers entirely for `registry.internal` patterns.

alex: long term: add DNS health probes for the internal forwarders and integrate with autoscaler so we don't provision GPU nodes into subnets with degraded DNS. Also consider moving critical image registry behind an IP that doesn't rely on split-horizon (TLS SNI + internal IP in LB).

omar: immediate plan: (1) infra to expand NAT port pool + revert aggressive port reuse (2) patch node bootstrap to ensure internal search first + ndots=2 for GPU-subnet (3) add a canary job that pulls a small image at node provision to validate DNS before bootstrapping heavy workloads. I'll open a PR for the bootstrap change.

sre-bot: update: infra expanded NAT ports and deployed config at 1977654390 UTC.

omar: after NAT change I'm seeing far fewer SERVFAILs in the next 5m — provisioning success rate back to normal. marking this as mitigated. will follow up with postmortem on root cause + long term fixes. :thumbsup:

katie: please add the canary job to cluster-autoscaler hooks and add the ndots change to the GPU AMI bake.

alex: thanks team — filed follow-up tickets: `ENGINFRA-4322` (canary), `ENGINFRA-4323` (bootstrap ndots/search), `INFRA-2107` (NAT port pool sizing).

omar: closing thread for now, will post postmortem once we have logs + root cause analysis.
